parameters.name: Injector duty cycle
parameters.notes: Above ~85% the injectors are near static — stop adding fuel, fix hardware. Formula assumes one injection event per cylinder per 2 crank revs (sequential on LS1). Map IPW/RPM to your actual VCM Scanner channel PIDs.
parameters.source: Community-standard formula — verify against your own scanner/logs

assumes.requires: Pulse width in MILLISECONDS. A scanner reporting microseconds gives a result 1000x high.

parameters.name: Total fuel trim
parameters.inputs: Long term fuel trim (%), Short term fuel trim (%)
parameters.notes: The combined correction the PCM is applying. Use per-bank versions to spot bank-to-bank differences (exhaust leak, injector). Target within ±5% after MAF cal.
parameters.source: Community-standard formula — verify against your own scanner/logs

assumes.requires: Both trims as percentages, not multipliers. A trim reported as 1.05 rather than 5% makes this meaningless.

parameters.name: MAF correction multiplier
parameters.notes: Histogram this against MAF frequency (Hz) to see how much to scale each MAF table cell. Multiply the current g/s value by the cell average. Closed loop, warmed up, no PE — filter your log accordingly.
parameters.source: Community-standard formula — verify against your own scanner/logs

assumes.requires: Both trims as percentages. Output is a multiplier to apply to the MAF table cell.

parameters.name: AFR error (wideband)
parameters.inputs: Wideband AFR, Commanded AFR (or lambda pair)
parameters.notes: Only meaningful once a wideband is installed. Positive = leaner than commanded. Prefer lambda over AFR to stay fuel-blend agnostic.
parameters.source: Community-standard formula — verify against your own scanner/logs

assumes.requires: BOTH inputs must use the same scale. The formula is scale-invariant — AFR against AFR and λ against λ give the identical answer — but λ measured against AFR commanded yields about -93%, which looks like a plausible rich reading rather than an error.
